title: fix(pm): dispatch-gates derives the gates that load a changed scripts/pm module, transitively
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9MG4BPhsDcJCksmNwyRu6xu)_

Fixes #33848

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:派发工具 `dispatch-gates.mjs` 新增「import 图」匹配键:改动落在 `scripts/pm/**` 下的某个模块时,所有直接或间接 import(含动态 import、再导出)它的门禁脚本所属的门禁族都会被派生出来,输出里打印从门禁脚本到该模块的整条 import 链。
- 为什么改:PR #33804 第一版只改了 `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` 和 `check-governed-merges.mjs`,`--commands` 派生 35 条、漏了 `check:pm-fleet-write-execute`(它的脚本 import 了被改的函数),开发者「35 条全绿」而 CI 红。现在同一组文件派生 62 条,含 fleet-write 的执行器、校验器和派发器。
- 风险与回滚:只改 `scripts/pm/**` 下一个工具脚本和它的自测,不发布任何包。新键排在所有旧键之后,旧匹配的键与来源标签一字不变,只会多派、不会少派;代价是改大多数 pm 模块会多派约 40 多个门禁族(pm 工具互相 import 成一个大环,这是实测的真实影响面)。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看:`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` 的 `loadEdgeTargets`(读 import 边,含动态 import 的兜底)与 `coveringKey` 末尾的新分支;自测文件里 `The import-graph key (#33848)` 一节和改过的两条旧用例。
- 两分钟验证:`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs | grep fleet-write`,预期三行 `pnpm check:pm-fleet-write-{dispatch,execute,validate}`(修复前零行)。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地(非受管面)。

## What changes

`dispatch-gates --commands` named a gate when a changed path was the gate's own script, a CI trigger, a job filter, a literal the gate spells, or a file it reads. It never named a gate because its script **imports** the changed module: `coveringKey`'s docblock refused that key (#13126) on precision, because the shared heads under `scripts/` (`invoked-as.mjs` and four others) are imported by most families. The pm tools are the opposite shape, and the measured miss is the card's: on PR #33804's first head the derivation named 35 gates, not `check:pm-fleet-write-execute`, whose script imports a changed function and whose self-test then went red in CI.

A new key, consulted **last** in `coveringKey`, answers a changed path under `IMPORT_GRAPH_KEY_ROOT` (`scripts/pm/`): a family matches when the path is in the transitive load closure of its gate files. Read from the module's side that is the reverse import graph over `scripts/pm/**`, at any depth. The row prints the chain, e.g. `import graph scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs -> scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`. Outside `scripts/pm/` the #13126 refusal stands unchanged (a self-test row pins that).

| Piece | What it does |
|:--|:--|
| `loadEdgeTargets(path, source)` | One file's first-party load edges: static `import … from`, `export … from` (a re-export loads its target), the side-effect form, a dynamic `import()` of a string literal or of `new URL(literal, import.meta.url)`. Comments are masked; a keyword inside a string or template literal is fixture text, not a load. Self-test bodies are **not** masked: a `--self-test` run loads them. |
| Unreadable dynamic `import()` | The argument is a variable, a property or a computed URL. It is not dropped: every code-position module literal in that file becomes an edge, whether relative or spelled from the repo root under `scripts/` (toward deriving more). Both shapes are live: a loader seam (`load = (specifier) => import(specifier)`) with its relative specifiers in a constant (`ARM_READER_SOURCE`), and a root-spelled roster loaded in process (`fleet-write/dispatch.mjs`'s self-test imports each sender through `pathToFileURL(join(REPO_ROOT, sender))`; `check-dispatch-gates.mjs` loads its engine through `import(resolve(ROOT, TOOL))`). The root spelling also takes fixture rows and text reads written the same way (five modules `check-governed-merges.mjs` names as data); that over-derives, which is this key's direction. |
| `importGraphReach(files, edgesOf)` | Breadth-first forward closure from a family's gate files, recording each module's first importer, so the printed chain is a shortest one. Walks self-test families and gate files too: the key claims what RUNNING the family loads, never what it watches, so neither population narrowing applies. |
| `discoverFamilies` | Computes `entry.importReach` for every family, one scan per file per discovery. |
| `derivationInputs` | Adds every reached module, since its edges decide what the key names. |

Resolution is the existing first-party rule: relative specifiers only, inside `scripts/`, outside `node_modules`, the target must exist. A bare specifier is an installed package.

Measured on this tree (b8685e50), and printed by a self-test row on every run rather than recorded in prose: the key reaches 28 pm modules over 1195 (family, module) pairs, and the most-reached module, `clause2-line.mjs`, names 53 families. The pm tools close into one large cycle (the governed register, the half-state patrol, the queue guard and the dispatch-gates engine load one another), so an edit to most pm modules names forty-odd families. That is the measured size of what such an edit can break.

Time, measured on a quiet container, two cold runs each: a discovery took 16.6 s and 14.8 s before the key (base e71ecc1b) and 17.2 s and 17.0 s with it (6f34ab17); a whole `--commands` run over one pm path took 36.0 s and 37.0 s before and 38.0 s and 35.7 s after. The review's 48.7 s was the same run on a loaded box. The stale "~14 s cold" in `derivationInputs`' docblock now carries these readings.

## Tests

Full battery (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --self-test`, both tiers) on b8685e50: **2530 cases pass** (fast 2215 + slow 315), lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`. Round 1: 2528 passed on 80bc14b0 and on e6452d31.

New rows, all in the fast tier:

- Fixture graph (in memory, so the shapes cannot rot with the tree): the reader takes the static import, the re-export, the side-effect form, a literal `import()` inside a self-test body and a `new URL` import; it refuses an import spelled in a template literal or a comment and a bare package; an unread `import()` widens to every module literal in the file, relative or root-spelled; CONTROL: the same two literals in a file with no unread `import()` are no edges.
- ⭐ Transitive row: in the fixture, `b.mjs` reached only through `gate.mjs -> a.mjs -> b.mjs` names the family, and the row prints that chain.
- Scope row: a module outside `scripts/pm/` reached by import is still answered by no key.
- ⭐ Root-spelled roster row (live tree, review M1): `scripts/pm/issue-create.mjs`, which no file under `scripts/` imports statically and which the dispatcher's self-test loads by root path, derives `check:pm-fleet-write-dispatch` through the import graph.
- Price row: prints the modules the key reaches, the (family, module) pairs and the most-reached module, asserting only that the key reaches anything.
- ⭐ Replay row (live tree): PR #33804's first file list places `check:pm-fleet-write-execute` as matched via `import graph scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs -> …`, rendered `pnpm check:pm-fleet-write-execute`; and `check:pm-fleet-write-validate` and `check:pm-fleet-write-dispatch` match too.

Forced edits to existing rows (both are about the key order this PR extends):

1. **The #13126 witness** (`the witness holds — bare-root-worklist --self-test imports THIS file, and no key names that family…`) asserted the refusal's one known missing lead. That module is under `scripts/pm/`, so the new key names it; the row now asserts the edge exists AND the key that names it is the import-graph key (`the witness is paid back — …`). The other five refusal pins (novel class, worst head, concentration, the deferred-pair pins) are unchanged and green.
2. **Read-key additivity** (`every read edge earns a key, and none is re-attributed …`) stripped `entry.reads` and compared against the keys left. The new key now sits after the read key, so with the reads stripped it answered those targets and the row reported 7 false re-attributions (`program text read by …` -> `import graph …`). The row now strips `entry.importReach` too, so it compares the read key against the keys consulted BEFORE it, which is its claim.

<details><summary>Ablation: the new branch in coveringKey disabled on disk, exactly the four key rows red, restored (head e6452d31)</summary>

Through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hits 1 -> 0 on disk, blob `7d65b7fe4962` -> `09197c9f6da0`), the fast tier under `os-verify-lock.sh`; restore: blob == HEAD (`7d65b7fe4962`) and `git diff HEAD` empty.

```text
mutation: the import-graph branch's condition prefixed with `false &&`
  -> VERDICT command-exit 1, 4 of 2213 failed:
  the witness is paid back — bare-root-worklist --self-test imports THIS file, and the import-graph key names that family for a card editing it
  the transitive row: a module reached only through an importer of an importer names the family, and the row prints the chain from the gate file
  the replay row: PR #33804's first file list derives check:pm-fleet-write-execute, through the import graph
  …and the validator and the dispatcher, the other two fleet-write families the card names
  (the edge-reader rows and the scope row stay green, as they must: they do not read the key)
```

</details>

<details><summary>Ablation, round 2 (review M1): the root-spelled half of the fallback disabled on disk, exactly two rows red, restored (head b8685e50)</summary>

Through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hits 1 -> 0, blob `8e00e6752a69` -> `fcd7324b7a64`), the fast tier under `os-verify-lock.sh`; restore: blob == HEAD (`8e00e6752a69`) and `git diff HEAD` empty.

```text
mutation: a root-spelled literal in a file with an unreadable import() is skipped instead of admitted
  -> VERDICT command-exit 1, 2 of 2215 failed:
  an import() whose argument is not a literal widens toward MORE: every module literal in the file is an edge, relative or spelled from the repo root
  a sender the dispatcher loads by a root-spelled path derives check:pm-fleet-write-dispatch, through the import graph
```

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- Additive by construction: the key is the last one `coveringKey` consults, so every (family, path) pair an earlier key answered keeps its key and label; the 2,520 rows that existed before stay green except the two forced edits above.
- Price, stated rather than hidden: a card editing most `scripts/pm/` modules now derives about 62 commands where it derived about 30 (this PR's own card: 62). Every added row prints its import chain, so a reader can check why it is there.
- Not covered by this key: the import closure of a script a gate only SPAWNS as a child (`node scripts/pm/x.mjs`) is not walked; the existing run and read keys answer the spawned file itself where they apply. carrier: #34084.
- The related evidence the delta names (`check:adr-anchors` reddened by a fixture string on PR #33975) is a different mechanism: that family declares five hints (`docs/adr`, `scripts/adr-anchors`, its own script and two `CHANGELOG.md` files) and no whole-tree marker, while its scan reads the whole tree's text. Its population is under-declared; not fixed here. carrier: #34086.
- Serial: #34002 (dotAll in `triggerPatternRegex`, same file) is held and not folded in.

## Verification

Local subset on b8685e50 (round 2; main e71ecc1b merged in): `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 62 commands; 61 exit 0 and one exit 3 (each exit captured before any pipe). `--ran` with every line annotated `:: exit N`: **62 derived, 61 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED (derived from the recorded exit 3), 0 UNRUN**. `pnpm check:i18n-coverage` is derived only through the import graph (its self-test imports the engine): its self-test half passed, its scan half refused with exit 3 because the CLI build closure is not built here; declared to CI. No package touched, so no build closure and no package test is owed.
